Read-only code audit · October 14, 2026 · requested by Jack Heart

What still belongs in the Work-first app?

The largest useful cuts remove surviving Session inventory, old chat rendering and duplicated navigation/opening coordination. Keep the retained workspace, native surface, draft and authoritative-reader owners. This report makes no source change and grants no review or Flow approval.

Complete tracked-source inventory; conservative semantic conclusions. All 174 Swift files parsed with zero diagnostics, including inactive branches. Every explicit func and deinit also matched an independent token count per file. Generated functions, downstream clients and runtime dispatch are not resolved. KEEP preserves a justified owner; it does not certify every branch as live.

Ranked coherent cuts

1. Remove the Session inventory still reachable in Task details DELETE

WorkSurfaceView.taskDetail renders Waiting and Sessions groups with counts and primary/provider/membership rows. The details sheet mounts it from SessionsContentView. This contradicts the accepted no-inventory UX; it is reachable obsolete UI, not dead code.

Replacement owner: Primary retained conversation, explicit contextual Session links and shared Waiting/program status; retain SessionRecord, full membership, TaskHistoryView and disclosed raw diagnostics.

Risk: Do not lose access to a waiting secondary Session: keep an exact contextual opening path. TaskSessionGroups is exported and needs API disposition before removal.

2. Replace view-driven opening handoffs with one existing-owner handoff SIMPLIFY

SessionsContentView reacts separately to focusedPaneId, repositoryEntryReady, sessions and linkedSession, then openLinkedSession/openSession place content. WorkModel already owns request generations and SessionsWorkspaceRegistry owns retained panes. Preserve those owners; derive opening/terminal/needs-action display rather than storing another lifecycle.

Replacement owner: Existing WorkModel request identity → SessionsWorkspaceRegistry/SessionsStore → GhosttySurfacePool; stable workspace/header/pane structure and retained last-good WorkReading data.

Risk: High: async stale replies, duplicate acquisition, client takeover, remote routing and unsent drafts. Generation/incarnation fences are necessary mechanics, not disposable state. This is a proposed cut, not implemented or runtime-proven.

3. Delete the unmounted native chat-reference renderer and its exclusive tests DELETE

ReferenceTextView/ReferenceContext/ReferenceMessageTextView/ReferencePopover have no production mount outside their own file. Only ReferenceTextViewTests calls static helpers. Their AppKit callbacks are protected only while the owning renderer is mounted; this closed owner is not registered by sdef or app bootstrap. resolveGitHubBase is also uncalled.

Replacement owner: Retained native provider terminal for conversations; MarkdownBlocks for authored supporting material. Exported ChatReference parser remains unresolved until library obligations are checked.

Risk: Do not remove Reference-like DTOs or general attributed-text mechanics by name. UIKit-only SelectableTextView tests reference an absent production type and are historical, not active Mac proof.

4. Remove constant-nil Roadmap selection and reconnect Task clicks SIMPLIFY

RoadmapView has one initializer setting _selection = .constant(nil), yet its row callbacks assign selection and its focusedContent/workBreadcrumb/taskCard depend on non-nil. The Portfolio window still mounts RoadmapView, so deleting the entire file would remove real UI. Its Task-click assignments currently cannot navigate.

Replacement owner: Existing WavesView.openTask / repository Work navigation; keep shared legal actions, Portfolio configuration and a useful overview.

Risk: Preserve access to cross-repository work. Remove dead focused branches only while wiring Task taps to the real destination; a new selection store repeats the old split ownership.

5. Remove obsolete presentation mode and stale UI-test paths SIMPLIFY

WorkNavigation.presentation defaults compact and only tests assign full; no sidebar presentation menu remains. UI tests still request work-presentation, Sessions and session-row-*; a native proof still taps debug-session-row-* despite production removal. DesktopPerformanceTests.measureWriteToVisible and measure(population:...) also locate the removed Picker, so previous performance journeys are not current acceptance evidence.

Replacement owner: One sidebar outline rule with collapse/search and unchanged retained membership; navigate tests through Work or explicit links.

Risk: Do not delete retention/input tests just because their old entry path is obsolete; retarget their behavior. Keep incomplete-planning and collapsed-Wave recovery coverage.

6. Move remaining authored-Wave discovery and creation behind lf SIMPLIFY

PortfolioService already uses the lf Portfolio API. Separately, PortfolioDiscovery enumerates GOAL.md, WavesView calls WavePlanParser.objective and PortfolioRepoState.createWave writes GOAL.md/MEMORY.md. This is live split planning ownership, not a Swift SQLite reader.

Replacement owner: Rust planning/authored-Wave read and create APIs through RegistryQuery; keep explicit path validation, existing PortfolioService and historical/authored-but-unregistered evidence.

Risk: Do not remove local discovery before the shared API exposes authored-only Waves and errors. No live data migration or filesystem cleanup follows from this audit.

8. Reconcile build/resource contracts and remove stale documentation SIMPLIFY

SwiftPM enables/pins GhosttyKit, while project.yml has neither its binary dependency nor GHOSTTY_ENABLED. The disabled implementations are therefore reachable build variants. README still describes selected-skill New Session, named-Session search and old Wave Chat. DESIGN carries obsolete shortcut/prompt-authority guidance.

Replacement owner: One explicit supported build/resource contract; retain pinned patches, fonts, sdef, entitlements and shell payload until parity is established.

Risk: Do not delete fallback terminal declarations solely because SwiftPM does not use them. No build/install or UI execution was performed in this audit. StatusColors.swift mixes unused aliases with the live Color(hex:) initializer: never delete the whole file based on alias use.

Owners to preserve

  • SessionsWorkspaceRegistry, MultiplexerStore and GhosttySurfacePool own retained panes, layouts and native clients. Hiding chrome must not destroy them.
  • TaskFileDocument and TaskFilesStore own unsaved documents. Keep their save/conflict behavior and location identity.
  • WorkModel/WorkReading and WorkCache already retain successful planning with explicit failure/staleness. publishRoadmap is a useful shared decision boundary.
  • RegistryQuery/RegistryQueryLocal call lf. No production Swift SQLite reader was found; filesystem-authored Wave discovery/writes are a distinct live boundary issue.
  • ScriptCommands is registered in Loopflow.sdef, LoopflowApp is @main, TestHostTerminator is a bundle principal class, and Ghostty/AppKit/FSEvents callbacks are runtime entry points.
  • ContextExplanation, SessionEvent, LfProcess and other lightly used DTOs remain published-wire/fixture contracts. Lack of active UI consumption does not authorize field deletion.
  • Color.init(hex:alpha:) in StatusColors.swift is live. The unused status aliases do not justify deleting that file.
  • Task history and disclosed raw diagnostics remain evidence, distinct from the obsolete ordinary Session inventory. Contextual exact-Session links remain a recovery/access path.

Counts include 151 initializers, 5 deinitializers, 473 implicit getters, 14 explicit accessors, 1 subscript, 46 extensions and 2,671 closures. The 7,432 binding entries include stored properties and local values; these are not 7,432 functions. Closures include builder and synchronous data-transform closures as well as callbacks.

Apple Swift 6.2.3 host SwiftParser/SwiftSyntax/SwiftParserDiagnostics; Parser.parse(source:) + recursive children(viewMode: .all), all #if/#elseif/#else branches. No diagnostics or parse-error nodes. Token cross-check: 1,812 func keywords and 5 deinit keywords, zero per-file mismatches.

  • Not a typechecked AST, compiler index, linker graph or execution trace; overloads, generic dispatch, protocol witnesses and aliases are not resolved.
  • Compiler-synthesized memberwise initializers, Codable/Hashable/Observable implementations, property-wrapper projections, result-builder transformations and expanded test/preview macro bodies are not separately enumerated. Their explicit owners/macros are covered; generated function completeness is not claimed.
  • A destructuring pattern is one binding entry, not one entry per bound identifier. Parameters, capture-list elements and closure parameters are signature content, not separately declared-function symbols.
  • Implicit getters are explicit inventory rows with the property binding range; they do not have separate source function declarations. Conditional paths record lexical branch clauses, not evaluated availability.
  • Closure call context is the nearest enclosing call expression; builder closures are included and are not all asynchronous callbacks.
  • Lexical reference index includes comments, strings, declaration sites and overload collisions. Empty references cannot prove deadness; dynamic owners are protected explicitly.
  • All tracked Swift/support files are inventoried. Semantic whole-program exhaustiveness is not claimed. Generic KEEP entries use conservative role/reference evidence, not a claim of individual runtime verification.
  • No app build, test suite, install, native rendering, DB read/write or external API probe was run. Binary resources are hashed/accounted for, not decoded.

Reference evidence: the complete lexical Swift occurrence index is included in JSON. Each entry points to candidate callers with file/line and enclosing callable. It includes comments, strings and overload collisions, and is explicitly not a resolved call graph. Per-entry displayed examples are bounded; the complete indexed occurrences are not. External build/docs matches are supporting evidence only.

Classification totals: KEEP 13457, UNRESOLVED 183, SIMPLIFY 638, DELETE 205. File classifications are aggregate decisions and may mix preserved mechanics with a proposed cut. A descendant can inherit its closed owner’s deletion decision; that is not a separate independent reachability proof.

Not run: app builds, test suites, display sessions, native input, database operations, installs or publication. Validation is parsing, declaration-token parity, path/range/ID coverage, source hashes and HTML/JSON structure. Only the two requested scratch artifacts are written. The parent rendering-state proposal is untouched.
